speaker: Narrator
text: For two years, you haven't seen the sky.

speaker: Narrator
text: Every month, a box shows up on the hatch. Food. Water filters. And a note. Always the same two words.

speaker: Narrator
text: Not yet.

speaker: Narrator
text: Today, the note changed.

speaker: Narrator
text: Two years ago, the rain turned green. And everyone it touched... stopped answering.

speaker: Lily
text: Max... who's been leaving the boxes?

speaker: Max
text: I don't know.

speaker: Narrator
text: Someone up there has fed you every month for two years. And today... they want you to come out.

speaker: Crane
text: Ladies and gentlemen... the cleanest power in America! Crane Power. Tomorrow, the switch goes on!

speaker: Anchor
text: Billionaire Victor Crane says the new plant will power three states.

speaker: Narrator
text: Your dad helped build that plant. Normally he'd be yelling 'that's my valve!' at the TV.

speaker: Narrator
text: Tonight, he hasn't touched his food.

speaker: Max
text: Dad. You okay?

speaker: Dad
text: Hm? Yeah, bud. Long day.

speaker: Narrator
text: Your mom is a nurse. She's on the night shift, so she sings Lily to sleep over the phone.

speaker: Mom
text: Little light, little light... stay with me tonight.

speaker: Lily
text: Again.

speaker: Mom
text: That's three times, missy. Goodnight. Max, you're in charge.

speaker: Narrator
text: Your dad puts a note in your lunch bag for tomorrow. Same as every day. 'Good luck, bud.' With a little star drawn inside the O.

speaker: Narrator
text: Then he does something he has never done.

speaker: Dad
text: Max. Look at me.

speaker: Dad
text: If the rain ever turns green... you take Lily to Grandpa's bunker. You close the hatch. And you don't open it for anybody.

speaker: Max
text: Green? Dad, what are you...

speaker: Dad
text: Promise me. And don't wait for us.

speaker: Max
text: Okay. I promise.

speaker: Narrator
text: He hangs a key around your neck. On a red string.

speaker: Narrator
text: Most dads just say 'drive safe.'

speaker: Narrator
text: The next day, the switch goes on at noon.

speaker: Narrator
text: At three ten, you're walking Lily home and arguing about whether a hot dog is a sandwich.

speaker: Lily
text: It's a taco. It's bread on one side.

speaker: Max
text: That's not how tacos work!

speaker: Narrator
text: At three twelve... the sky changes color.

speaker: Lily
text: Max. Why is the sky green?

speaker: Narrator
text: The clouds over the plant are glowing. Like a soda can held up to the sun.

speaker: Narrator
text: A bird drops off the power line. It doesn't flap. It just... drops.

speaker: Max
text: Lily. Hold my hand.

speaker: Lily
text: What's wrong?

speaker: Narrator
text: The first drop hits the sidewalk. It hisses. The grass next to it turns black.

speaker: Max
text: Run!

speaker: Narrator
text: Four houses. Three. Mrs. Patel is standing in her yard, looking up, smiling, holding out her hand to catch it.

speaker: Max
text: Mrs. Patel! Get inside!

speaker: Lily
text: Mister Buttons! I dropped Mister Buttons!

speaker: Max
text: Leave him! Lily, leave him!

speaker: Narrator
text: The backyard. The hatch. The key on the red string. Your hands are shaking so hard it takes three tries.

speaker: Narrator
text: The rain hits the lid one second after it closes.

speaker: Narrator
text: Grandpa built this bunker in nineteen sixty-two, for a war that never came.

speaker: Narrator
text: He stocked it like he expected the war to last forever. Four hundred cans of beans. One can opener.

speaker: Lily
text: Is Mom coming?

speaker: Max
text: Yeah. Yeah, they're coming. They're just... waiting for the rain to stop.

speaker: Anchor
text: A toxic weather event over the tri-state area. Residents are told to stay indoors.

speaker: Crane
text: This is Victor Crane. Please don't panic. This is a temporary event. Crane Power has everything under control.

speaker: Narrator
text: People who have everything under control don't usually say it twice.

speaker: Crane
text: Everything is under control.

speaker: Narrator
text: At nine forty that night, your phone finds one bar. One voicemail.

speaker: Mom
text: Max, it's Mom. I'm at the hospital, they're bringing in so many people. Don't go outside. Whatever happens, keep her...

speaker: Narrator
text: Then the bar is gone.

speaker: Lily
text: Play it again.

speaker: Narrator
text: You play it again. And again. Until the battery dies.

speaker: Jayden
text: Max! Max, you there? Over!

speaker: Max
text: Jayden?! You're alive!

speaker: Jayden
text: I'm in the attic. My mom's stuck at work. Dude, the whole street looks like a sci-fi movie. Over.

speaker: Narrator
text: Jayden lives four houses down. Every night, he climbs to his attic window and counts the houses with lights on.

speaker: Jayden
text: Eleven lights. Over.

speaker: Narrator
text: Day four.

speaker: Jayden
text: Six lights left on our street. Over.

speaker: Narrator
text: Day nine.

speaker: Jayden
text: Two. Yours and mine. Over.

speaker: Narrator
text: Day twelve.

speaker: Jayden
text: Max... my battery's almost dead. If you get out... tell my mom I was brave, okay? Even if I wasn't.

speaker: Max
text: Jayden. Jayden, don't...

speaker: Narrator
text: You keep the walkie on for a week. It never says another word.

speaker: Narrator
text: Then, on day thirty, something knocks on the hatch.

speaker: Narrator
text: Three knocks. Then footsteps... walking away.

speaker: Lily
text: Is it Mom?

speaker: Narrator
text: You check Grandpa's periscope. There's no one there. Just a wooden box.

speaker: Narrator
text: You wait until the rain stops. Then you open the hatch just wide enough to pull it in.

speaker: Max
text: Food. Water filters. Batteries...

speaker: Lily
text: Mister Buttons!

speaker: Narrator
text: The rabbit she dropped in the street. Washed. Clean. It smells like soap.

speaker: Narrator
text: Someone walked into your yard... in the poison rain... and picked him up.

speaker: Max
text: There's a note. 'Not yet.'

speaker: Lily
text: It's Mom. I know it's Mom.

speaker: Narrator
text: But then you see the side of the box. A logo. A lightning bolt in a circle.

speaker: Max
text: Crane Power.

speaker: Narrator
text: The people who made the rain are the ones feeding you.

speaker: Narrator
text: Every thirty days, three knocks. A box. Two words.

speaker: Narrator
text: You learn the rules of the bunker the hard way. The water filter lasts nine days, not ten. Beans taste better cold, if you pretend they're chili.

speaker: Lily
text: They don't.

speaker: Narrator
text: They don't.

speaker: Narrator
text: Lily learns to read from the labels on the boxes. Her first word is 'perishable.' Her second word is 'Crane.'

speaker: Lily
text: P, E, R, I... perishable!

speaker: Narrator
text: On day two hundred fourteen, there's something new at the bottom of the box.

speaker: Max
text: A candle?

speaker: Lily
text: Max. Today's the ninth.

speaker: Narrator
text: Her birthday. Nobody in the world knows her birthday. Except family.

speaker: Max
text: Make a wish.

speaker: Lily
text: I wish whoever it is... could come inside.

speaker: Narrator
text: Day two-sixty, the air alarm starts beeping.

speaker: Narrator
text: Grandpa's air vent comes up behind the shed. Something is blocking it. And outside, it's raining.

speaker: Lily
text: You can't go up there!

speaker: Max
text: If I don't, we both stop breathing in about six hours.

speaker: Narrator
text: Two raincoats. Six trash bags. Duct tape. Ski goggles. You look like a burrito going to war.

speaker: Max
text: If I'm not back in ten minutes... lock the hatch.

speaker: Lily
text: Don't say that!

speaker: Narrator
text: You climb out into the green.

speaker: Narrator
text: The town is silent. Cars stopped in the middle of the road. Doors open. A soccer ball floating in a green puddle.

speaker: Narrator
text: Vines have grown over the vent. You rip them out with both hands.

speaker: Narrator
text: And then you see them in the mud. Boot prints. Big ones. Coming from your house... and going toward the plant.

speaker: Narrator
text: One drop finds the gap in your glove.

speaker: Max
text: Ah!

speaker: Narrator
text: You make it back down in eight minutes.

speaker: Narrator
text: By night, you're burning with fever.

speaker: Lily
text: Okay. Okay. The book says... keep the patient hydrated.

speaker: Narrator
text: For five days, your eight-year-old sister runs the bunker. She changes the filter. She rations the beans. She sings you Mom's song, off-key.

speaker: Lily
text: Little light, little light... stay with me tonight.

speaker: Narrator
text: And on the second night, she does something brave. She writes a note, climbs the ladder, and sticks it on the outside of the hatch.

speaker: Lily
text: My brother is sick. Please.

speaker: Narrator
text: The next morning... there are no knocks. It's not day thirty. But there's a box.

speaker: Lily
text: Medicine!

speaker: Narrator
text: And a different note. Written fast, like a hand that couldn't stop shaking.

speaker: Lily
text: Hold on.

speaker: Narrator
text: When your fever breaks, you read it yourself. And you see it.

speaker: Narrator
text: A little star... drawn inside the O.

speaker: Max
text: Dad?

speaker: Narrator
text: Lily says you're crazy. Dad would come inside. Dad would open the hatch.

speaker: Lily
text: If it was Dad, why won't he come in?!

speaker: Max
text: I don't know!

speaker: Narrator
text: So on day three hundred, you don't sleep. You sit at the periscope all night.

speaker: Narrator
text: At three A.M., a figure walks out of the rain.

speaker: Narrator
text: Gas suit. Mask. A box in its arms. And on its back, the lightning bolt. Crane Power.

speaker: Narrator
text: It sets down the box. It puts a gloved hand flat on the hatch. And it just... stays there. For a long time.

speaker: Max
text: That's not Dad.

speaker: Lily
text: How do you know?

speaker: Max
text: Because Dad would never wear that. Crane took him. And now Crane copies his notes to keep us down here. So we can't tell anyone what happened.

speaker: Narrator
text: Lily doesn't answer. She just keeps holding Mister Buttons.

speaker: Narrator
text: The second year is quieter.

speaker: Narrator
text: Victor Crane's radio messages stop in March. Nobody says why.

speaker: Narrator
text: You grow tomatoes under the lamp from seeds in box number eleven. Lily names every single one.

speaker: Lily
text: That's Gerald. That's Big Gerald.

speaker: Narrator
text: The tally marks fill one wall. Then a second.

speaker: Narrator
text: You're fifteen now. Lily is ten. She doesn't remember what Mom's face looks like without the voicemail. So you tell her, every night.

speaker: Max
text: She had a laugh like a hiccup. And she always smelled like hospital soap.

speaker: Lily
text: Like Mister Buttons did.

speaker: Narrator
text: Twenty-three boxes. Twenty-three notes. 'Not yet.'

speaker: Narrator
text: Until day seven thirty-one.

speaker: Narrator
text: Now.

speaker: Lily
text: What if it's a trick?

speaker: Max
text: Then I want to see his face.

speaker: Narrator
text: You open the hatch all the way. For the first time in two years.

speaker: Narrator
text: The sky is blue.

speaker: Narrator
text: The town is green, but the good kind. Vines on the stop signs. Grass through the road. A deer standing in the middle of Main Street like it pays rent.

speaker: Lily
text: It's so... quiet.

speaker: Narrator
text: And on every corner, drawn in white chalk... an arrow. With a star inside the O of the word 'this way.'

speaker: Narrator
text: The arrows lead three miles. To the one building you never wanted to see again.

speaker: Max
text: Crane Power.

speaker: Narrator
text: The doors are welded shut, except one. Inside, it's warm. There's a hum. Someone has kept the lights on.

speaker: Narrator
text: In the control room, a man in a gas suit is standing at the window, looking at your town.

speaker: Max
text: Where's my dad?!

speaker: Narrator
text: You're holding a pipe. You don't remember picking it up.

speaker: Max
text: What did you do to my dad?!

speaker: Narrator
text: He takes off the mask.

speaker: Narrator
text: Gray beard. Thin. Older than two years should make anyone.

speaker: Dad
text: Hey, bud.

speaker: Lily
text: Daddy!

speaker: Dad
text: I tested the new gas for Crane. Three weeks before the launch. I told him it reacted with water vapor. I told him what it would do to rain.

speaker: Dad
text: He told me to sign the safety report anyway. Or lose everything.

speaker: Dad
text: And I signed it.

speaker: Dad
text: The day it rained, I ran to the main valve. I shut it down by hand. The room sealed behind me. The doors are built to lock when the gas leaks.

speaker: Dad
text: I had one suit. One filter a month. Enough for one trip. Enough to reach you, put down a box... and come back.

speaker: Max
text: You were right there. Why didn't you come in?!

speaker: Dad
text: Because opening that hatch, even for a second, would let the rain in. On you. On her.

speaker: Dad
text: So I stood on top of it. Every month. And I wrote 'not yet.' Because every box was me saying sorry.

speaker: Max
text: Where's Mom?

speaker: Dad
text: She was at the hospital. I went there every month for a year. I never found her.

speaker: Max
text: You told me not to wait for you.

speaker: Dad
text: And you didn't. That's why she's alive.

speaker: Narrator
text: The plant's old radio has been on for two years. Static. Every day. Nothing.

speaker: Narrator
text: Today, it clicks.

speaker: Shelter
text: This is Shelter Four. If anyone can hear us... we have forty survivors. We have food. Please...

speaker: Narrator
text: And behind the voice, very quiet... someone is humming.

speaker: Mom
text: Little light, little light... stay with me tonight.

speaker: Lily
text: That's Mom.

speaker: Narrator
text: The rain kept you apart for two years. Now you have three miles of sunlight... and one radio signal.

speaker: Narrator
text: And Victor Crane is still out there somewhere.

speaker: Narrator
text: Part two. What If You Found the Last Shelter?
